reading: A: a worker claims the key and dies -> the caller gets HTTP 500 whose entire body is `Internal Server Error`, and the durable row stays response_status=NULL

B/C: replaying that dead key answers 409 `agent idempotency record is incomplete` after about 800 ms of waiting, and the row is still NULL on the third attempt -> the key is burned for the rest of its receipt life

D/E: a key held by a *healthy* worker shows the identical NULL row, and the replay is answered with the same 409 and the same envelope (C/E third element true) -> in-flight and dead cannot be told apart from the response
F/G: that healthy worker finished with 201 and a later replay of the same key returns 201 in 16 ms -> the 409 handed out while it ran was simply wrong
H: a never-used key still returns 201, so the route is not broken in general
body_comparison_basis: trace_id is regenerated per call, so equality is judged with trace_id normalised; raw byte equality is false by construction
instrument_note: the first pass ran the slow holder without CITYNEXUS_DATABASE_URL, so it opened ./citynexus.db and cells D to G were void; only the corrected pass is quoted

premise_for_reclaim_safety.not_covered_by_this_premise: an external AI or Hermes call made inside the dead attempt stays out there - that is ORD-0270 EXTERNAL_EFFECT_NOT_ROLLBACKABLE, and a lease does not undo it

touch_set.why_main_py_is_unavoidable: the claim writer, the fill guard, the waiting reader and the route that turns an outcome into an HTTP answer all live in backend/app/main.py, the file the order itself names as lane F's land while ORD-0332 runs there
touch_set.why_one_new_durable_column: idempotency_keys carries only expires_at, which means receipt validity (+7 days here) and is deliberately not trusted as a guard; a lease deadline is a different clock and reusing that column would make 'reclaim' and 'forget' the same value

proposal.lease: each attempt carries a token plus claim_deadline; the deadline is derived from the configured write budget rather than invented, so it cannot expire while a legitimate attempt can still finish

named_states.PLAN_GENERATION_IN_FLIGHT: an unexpired lease is held by someone else, retry_after_ms says when to come back, nothing is burned
named_states.PLAN_GENERATION_ATTEMPT_STALE: the lease lapsed with a NULL receipt; the caller may take over. today this case is indistinguishable from the one above

proposal.fencing: the fill becomes UPDATE ... WHERE response_json IS NULL AND claim_token = <my token>, so a resurrected original worker cannot overwrite the answer that replaced it
proposal.never_done: claim rows are never deleted and receipts never forgotten; recovery either reads the winner or takes over a lapsed attempt under a token
acceptance_cells: lease lapsed -> re-claim wins and the new answer lands
lease unexpired -> re-claim refused, and the refusal is the named in-flight code
the resurrected original tries to fill -> refused, and the winning answer survives
the dead-claim shape stops being permanent: the same key yields a real answer afterwards

sequencing_request: not a line of this is written until you order it. the edit lands in backend/app/main.py while F is in the same file for ORD-0332, so either F finishes and I rebase, or I land the lease first and F rebases. also say whether backend/app/db/session.py plus schema.sql may move with me in the same commit, because the lease needs one durable column.
demo_reset_invoked: against a declared throwaway database only, which is the fixture door the suite already uses; the live and preview targets were never opened
